question: Should generic tool-progress metadata become a supported public plugin-SDK reply-payload contract, or remain an internal contract used by bundled producers and channels?
rationale: The PR adds externally callable SDK surface while the repository policy favors narrow internal seams unless third-party plugin use is intentional; functional correctness alone cannot decide that API commitment.

options.title: Keep it internal
options.body: Use an internal generic reply metadata contract for bundled Codex and Slack until an external plugin requirement justifies a public API.

options.title: Approve the public contract
options.body: Retain the exported constant and predicate, document their semantics, and add focused compatibility tests for third-party consumers.

recommendation.title: Keep it internal
recommendation.body: Use an internal generic reply metadata contract for bundled Codex and Slack until an external plugin requirement justifies a public API.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects this person to narrowing and maintaining the public reply-payload SDK boundary.
